data.one_liner: A Flutter Pusher client for Laravel Reverb with custom paths and dynamic headers.
data.what_it_does: Provides real-time WebSocket communication using the Pusher Protocol optimized for Laravel Reverb. It supports public, private, and end-to-end encrypted channels alongside automatic reconnection.
use_when: You are building a Flutter application that connects to a Laravel Reverb backend.
You need real-time updates via public, private, or encrypted channels.
You want stream-based or callback-based event handling for WebSocket messages.
avoid_when: You are using WebSockets without a Pusher-compatible protocol or Laravel Reverb.
You require features tied to browser-specific WebSocket configurations that are unsupported on web.
strengths: Supports all Flutter platforms including Web, Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, and Linux.
Includes built-in support for encrypted channels with AES-256-CBC.
Automatic reconnection handling with exponential backoff.
weaknesses: API key connection headers and ping intervals are ignored on web due to browser limitations.
Early stage version (0.0.10) which may undergo API changes.
data.setup_notes: Requires a running Laravel backend with Reverb configured. Pass host, port, and appKey to initialize the client.
